title: Flying High or Falling Short? Markup and Product Differentiation in the U.S. Airline Industry
core_idea: Introduces a novel framework, building on the work of C.A.K. Lovell, to decompose annual markup changes while explicitly incorporating product differentiation as an economic driver; applies this methodology to analyze profitability dynamics across 20 U.S. airlines over a two-decade period.
tldr: Presents a markup-decomposition method that integrates product differentiation to study the drivers of industry- and firm-level profitability in the U.S. airline sector.
